verified: Registration and login use real HTTP requests with Bearer tokens.
Two accounts see only their own characters and cannot read the other account's character state.
A normal initial character wins and clears the first two campaign nodes using legal battle.command requests.
An identical request id replays its stored result, while reuse with a different payload is rejected.
Invalid actions and an insufficient-silver purchase leave revision, state, and balances unchanged.
Friend request and acceptance, private chat, mail attachment claim, direct trade, and auction buy work through real HTTP requests.
Mail, trade, and auction card quantities are conserved; successful trade and auction preserve combined player silver apart from the explicit mail postage checked before those exchanges.
Both player accounts issue real HTTP actions in a cooperative battle and receive winning settlement.
Both player accounts issue real HTTP actions in a ranked PVP battle; wins, losses, ratings, and ranking order settle consistently.
After closing and recreating the server on the same SQLite path, fresh logins recover progression, balances, friendship, completed trade, completed auction, and ranked ratings.
boundaries: The regression starts the imported createGameServer on a random loopback port.
All gameplay changes pass through public HTTP endpoints; the test does not edit the game database directly.
The temporary SQLite directory is deleted during test teardown.
No Cocos build or external deployment is part of this check.
